title: Impact of Remote Ischemic Conditioning on Free Flaps
summary: Free tissue transfer is a routine procedure in plastic surgery. However, perfusion disturbances can still lead to partial or complete flap failure. With regard to the current literature "remote ischemic conditioning (RIC)" has emerged to a promising tool to induce systemic protective effects against perfusion compromise and impaired wound healing in free flap tissue. RIC is mediated by simply inflating and deflating a standard blood pressure cuff placed on the upper arm. This study should contribute further evidence to the protective impact of RIC in free flap surgery.

interventions.name: Intervention group: RIC is performed by repetitively inflating and deflating a standard blood pressure cuff placed on the upper arm (three 10 min cuff inflations and deflations) one day preoperatively and intraoperatively during flap revascularization.
Control group: No RIC is performed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Free flap surgery
Exclusion criteria:
Children, patients with a health care proxy, contraindications for blood pressure cuff inflation (e.g. post-traumatic, vascular disease) or indocyanine-green fluorescence angiography (e.g. manifest hyperthyroidism, iodine allergy)
